nodes.label: Allelic Ratio (ASE)
nodes.rationale: Genes are called allele-specific when allelic_ratio <= 0.3 or >= 0.7 for the autosomal survey, but downstream link work uses a looser 0.35/0.65 window and a 0.65/0.70 reference threshold family. The dual thresholds exist because the ASE prevalence figure is descriptive (wide, conservative cut) while link calling must retain borderline-biased loci so that loss of bias can be distinguished from loss of expression.

nodes.label: Link Mechanism (enhancing vs repressing)
nodes.rationale: Every link carries a mechanism label so a lncRNA base and its pcGene target are treated as a directed pair. Mechanism is folded into the link identity key (base|target|mechanism) rather than kept as an attribute, which makes a mechanism flip register as a simultaneous loss and gain rather than a modified edge.

nodes.label: Gained / Lost / Retained Link Classification
nodes.rationale: Links are partitioned by set difference between adult and aged rather than by a statistical test, because there is no replicate structure at the link level. Concordance with expression fold change and a mechanism-shuffling permutation null are used instead to show the gains and losses are not arbitrary.

nodes.label: Mechanism-Shuffling Permutation Null
nodes.rationale: Only the mechanism labels are permuted, deliberately preserving base/target identity and their fold changes. This isolates the question 'is the enhancing/repressing call informative?' from confounding by which genes happen to be differentially expressed.

nodes.label: Expression Loss vs Mechanism Loss
nodes.rationale: A disappeared link is triaged into expression_loss (gene undetected or below a 50-read floor) versus mechanism_loss (gene still expressed but allelic ratio returned to balance). Without this split, links lost purely to dropout at low depth would be misread as genuine regulatory rewiring.

nodes.label: Noncoding Base to Coding Target Link Filter
nodes.rationale: Links are restricted to a noncoding RefSeq base acting on a protein-coding target, using the Refseq_coding_noncoding.txt lookup shared across scripts. Same-gene isoform links are also dropped, since two transcripts of one gene share allelic bias trivially and would inflate the link count.
nodes.norm_label: noncoding base to coding target link filter

nodes.label: Predicted vs No-Predicted Annotation and 65/70 Ratio Sweep
nodes.rationale: Four reference/threshold combinations (predicted vs no_predicted RefSeq annotation, crossed with 65:35 and 70:30 allelic cutoffs) are counted side by side so the eventual choice of no_predicted at 65 can be justified as a sensitivity result rather than an arbitrary default.
nodes.norm_label: predicted vs no-predicted annotation and 65/70 ratio sweep

nodes.label: Aging vs Pressure-Overload Injury Parallel
nodes.rationale: Aged-vs-adult and TAC-vs-sham are run as structurally identical contrasts so their effects can be correlated directly. Because the two come from separate studies, cross-study comparison is only done on limma batch-corrected VST values with condition protected in the design; raw counts are never compared across studies.

nodes.label: Per-Cell-Type Pseudobulk Fold Change
nodes.rationale: Counts are summed per cell type and age into a pseudobulk column and compared as a raw logCPM difference with no dispersion model. With one animal per condition there is no replicate to estimate dispersion from, so a descriptive log2FC is reported instead of a p-value.

nodes.label: Per-Link Logistic Age Model
nodes.rationale: Link presence is completed to a full subject x link grid (absences filled as 0) and modelled as binomial ~ AGE_collapsed with emmeans contrasts. Ages are collapsed to three bins because per-decade GTEx strata are too thin to fit; the completion step is essential or absent links would be silently dropped instead of counted as zeros.

nodes.label: Link Accumulation (Rarefaction) Curve
nodes.rationale: Unique links are accumulated over randomly ordered subjects across 200 permutations so that age groups with different sample sizes can be compared at matched sampling depth, rather than by raw total link counts which scale with cohort size.

nodes.label: Epigenetic Clock Gene Overlap (Horvath / PhenoAge / Hannum / Mouse CpG)
nodes.rationale: Age-changing links are intersected with published methylation-clock gene panels to test whether allelic rewiring lands on loci already known to track biological age, giving an independent anchor for what is otherwise an unreplicated set-difference result.
nodes.norm_label: epigenetic clock gene overlap (horvath / phenoage / hannum / mouse cpg)

nodes.label: Delta Gene-Gene Correlation Rewiring
nodes.rationale: Spearman correlation matrices are differenced (aged - adult and TAC - sham) over the top 2000 variable genes, and each edge scored by the product of absolute deltas. Restricting to variable genes keeps the pairwise edge space tractable while the joint score surfaces edges rewired by both aging and injury.

nodes.label: Bayesian Beta-Binomial Allelic Bias
nodes.rationale: Per-SNP allelic counts get a Beta prior posterior, with a strong Beta(10,10) prior on autosomes but a weak Jeffreys Beta(0.5,0.5) on chrX, because X-linked loci are expected to be genuinely monoallelic and a symmetric prior would shrink real skew toward 0.5. Scores are read-weighted so deeply covered SNPs dominate the gene-level call.

nodes.label: IGV Interact Track Encoding
nodes.rationale: Links are encoded as BEDPE with score +1/-1 and green/red RGB for enhancing/repressing, and locus tables as BED coloured in five allelic-ratio bins. The sign-as-score convention lets IGV's useScore rendering distinguish mechanism without a separate track.
